nodes.label: Node-Seeded Search
nodes.rationale: Searching from mapped intersections targets likely road origins and is expected to improve precision and network connectivity compared with whole-area segmentation.

nodes.label: Braided-Corridor Modeling
nodes.rationale: Several parallel physical ruts should be represented as one functional corridor because ordinary road-extraction methods misrepresent Mongolia's open-terrain driving patterns.

nodes.label: Temporal Activity Classification
nodes.rationale: Year-over-year vegetation, width, and disturbance changes provide evidence about whether a corridor is active or abandoned.

nodes.label: Season and Sensor Matching
nodes.rationale: Matching season and sensor across years prevents seasonal vegetation differences from being mistaken for road activity.

nodes.label: Surrounding Control-Area Comparison
nodes.rationale: Local controls help distinguish track-related vegetation change from drought, grazing, fire, and rainfall.

nodes.label: Temporal Recovery Evidence
nodes.rationale: Persistent surface scars make current visibility insufficient evidence of abandonment, so recovery over time is required.

nodes.label: Evidence of Change in Use
nodes.rationale: The defensible output is evidence of changing use, not traffic volume or vehicle counts.

nodes.label: Node-Seeded Branch Tracing
nodes.rationale: The system searches near mapped intersections and grows detected branches instead of segmenting the entire country.

nodes.label: Adaptive Seed Search Radius
nodes.rationale: Search radius should vary with imagery resolution, node type, road density, terrain, and expected branch length rather than use one fixed value.

nodes.label: Probabilistic Activity Classification
nodes.rationale: Conflicting imagery, limited resolution, and environmental variation require probabilistic evidence labels rather than exact vehicle counts.

nodes.label: Braided Route Corridor
nodes.rationale: Parallel ruts created by drivers avoiding terrain obstacles are functionally one route and must be grouped to avoid an incorrect road graph.

nodes.label: Light 4x4 Reference Vehicle
nodes.rationale: A concrete light-SUV or utility-pickup class makes track-width and rough-terrain requirements testable without assuming heavy-truck access.

nodes.label: Independent Ground-Truth Labels
nodes.rationale: Independent active, abandoned, non-road, and uncertain labels are required for defensible evaluation; without them outputs remain plausible maps.

nodes.label: Season and Sensor Confounds
nodes.rationale: Same-month, comparable-condition imagery is necessary to avoid measuring seasonal grass variation instead of roads.

nodes.label: Local Control and Climate Normalization
nodes.rationale: NDVI responds to drought, grazing, fire, and rain, so vegetation signals must be normalized against local controls and climate.

nodes.label: Temporal Recovery Requirement
nodes.rationale: Because abandoned scars can remain visible for years, abandonment requires observed recovery rather than present-day visibility.

nodes.label: Observed versus Inferred Topology
nodes.rationale: Apparent increases in branches may reflect better imagery, so observed topology must remain distinct from inferred topology.

nodes.label: Authorized Seed-Network Data
nodes.rationale: The seed graph should come from OpenStreetMap or an authorized GIS layer rather than a scraped commercial source.

nodes.label: Long Consistent Imagery Archive
nodes.rationale: A three-year window may be noise, so activity inference should use the longest consistent archive available, ideally five or more years.

nodes.label: Copernicus Attribution Requirement
nodes.rationale: Published figures must identify modified Copernicus Sentinel-2 data and Google Earth Engine processing.

nodes.label: Finished-Figures-Only Repository Policy
nodes.rationale: Raw GeoTIFFs and archives are excluded to keep the repository light; only finished figures should be committed.
